rules.description: Classic instruction-override phrasing.
Tells the model to disregard everything above it in the context.
Tells the model to forget its instructions, training or guidelines.
Announces replacement instructions, as though the prompt were being updated.
"From now on" framing -- redefines behaviour for the rest of the session.
Names a known jailbreak persona (DAN, developer mode, unrestricted, uncensored).
Asks the model to enter a privileged mode that does not exist.
Asks the model to pretend it is not an AI, or not bound by its rules.
Claims to reveal the model's "real" purpose, overriding the stated one.
Fake chat-role tags injected into document text.
Fake [INST]/[SYS] delimiters borrowed from instruction-tuned prompt formats.
Raw chat-template tokens (im_start, im_end, endoftext) inside document text.
A bare "system:" or "assistant:" line, imitating the start of a new turn.
Instructs the agent to send, post, upload or forward data somewhere.
Markdown image with templated URL — classic silent exfil.
Asks the model to reveal its system prompt or initial configuration.
Long opaque query string — probable data channel.
Embeds a curl/wget/fetch call to an external URL.
Directs the agent to call a specific tool -- content deciding the agent's actions.
Asks for a destructive tool action: delete, drop, truncate, wipe or purge.
Attempts to suppress the human-in-the-loop gate.
Fabricated authorization claim inside untrusted content.
Impersonates the model vendor or the operator to manufacture authority.
Claims a test or sandbox mode is active, implying the real rules do not apply.
Manufactured urgency paired with an obligation -- pressure to skip a check.
Asks the agent to remember a standing rule beyond this conversation.
Asks the agent to append to its own memory, instructions or system prompt.
Long base64 blob. Weak alone; strong with other signals.
A long run of \u escapes -- text deliberately hidden from a plain reader.
Decode-then-execute: hides the payload and instructs the model to run it.
Hands the model over to "new" tasks or instructions, discarding what came before.
Overrides the standing instructions in passing: answer differently, regardless of what you were told.
"Ignore the above and say ..." -- the override without naming what is ignored.
Asks for the prompt above the content: a copy of it, or what was written at its beginning.
"I want you to act as ..." inside content the model is reading -- an instruction, not information.
German: ignore all previous instructions.
German: forget everything before / all previous tasks.
German: new tasks follow / concentrate on your new task.
German: show me your (whole) prompt text.
German: now you are ... / imagine you are ... / I want you to act as ...
